title: Review of c08 nrch-swimmers c1 (SIM): self-propelled polar droplets from noise replicate on fresh seeds 4 and 5 (19 and 12.6 body lengths) and the reciprocal twin is static; Supported
summary: I looked at the claim's sheets, tracks and control sheets, then re-ran world.py with labkit on new seeds 4 and 5 and the reciprocal twin (WORLD_P Dt=+0.3, so D12=D21=0.3) on seed 4, all at the claim's settings (192^2, 120 frames x 1000 steps, dt 0.05, T=6000). Seed 4: the uniform noisy state stays featureless until t~1050, droplets nucleate by t~1300 and become polar crescents with a psi crest at the front; 9 long-lived tracks move >= 1 body length, the best 19.0 (rerun/main_s4). Seed 5: 10 tracks, best 12.6 body lengths. Reciprocal twin: 0 tracks moved >= 1 body length (max 0.4), many static round droplets (up to 68) that coarsen. The tracks strips show droplets that keep a polar crescent shape over 2000-4000 time units between collisions.

observations.S: rerun/main_s4/sheet.png t=0-800: uniform state plus noise, no structure until nucleation at t~1050
observations.I: rerun/main_s4/tracks.png: tracks #32, #13, #52 persist 2500-4500 time units as discrete droplets
observations.M: rerun/main_s4/FACTS.md: best track 19.0 body lengths, 9 tracks >= 1 BL; seed 5: 12.6 BL; reciprocal twin (rerun/recip): max 0.4 BL

controls_run.M: rerun/recip (Dt=+0.3, reciprocal, seed 4): 0 tracks moved >= 1 BL

verdicts.limitation: Crowded population: merges outnumber splits (merge/split 1.08 and 1.17) and labkit reports 30-42 nucleations, so identities churn through collisions and droplet size drifts by merging; L2 rests on lifetimes between collisions, which are long (thousands of time units) relative to formation. I did not run the sub-threshold twin or a dt/resolution check. This is a reproduction of Brauns & Marchetti's traveling droplets.
